question.text: Ms. Neha Raghavan, Head of IR at Saraswati Capital AIF, is drafting a Benchmarking Note for LPs and needs to articulate the primary function of a market index in modern investment management. Which of the following statements BEST captures what an index is and what it does in the AIF context?

answer.text: An index is a predictive model that forecasts future market returns based on GDP trends and interest rate expectations.
An index is a regulatory construct mandated by SEBI for computing the fair value of unlisted equity positions held by Category I AIFs.

An index is a composite measure that reflects the change in value of an underlying basket of securities from a base value, used as a gauge of the market, a benchmark for active managers, and the underlying portfolio for passive funds.
An index is solely a price-weighted arithmetic average of constituent securities, designed to track short-term trader sentiment on listed instruments.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 10.1 and 10.2 of the Chapter, an index is a composite measure that reflects the change in the value of underlying securities over time relative to a base value. Its documented uses are: (i) gauge of market performance, (ii) benchmark for actively managed portfolios, (iii) underlying portfolio for index funds (passive), and (iv) proxy for the market portfolio of risky assets in CAPM for measuring systematic risk. The Trap: Option A confuses an index (descriptive measure) with a forecasting model. Option B is false; SEBI does NOT mandate an index for AIF valuation (that is the role of the Valuation Agency under Reg 23). Option D limits indices to price-weighted only, ignoring value-weighted, equal-weighted, and fundamental-weighted variants. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B (PM) tests the CAPM proxy use of indices. XIX-A/B (Distributor) tests benchmark selection for client suitability. XV (Research Analyst) tests index methodology for sector research. Manager's Pro-Tip: When writing your PPM benchmark section, explicitly call out WHICH of these four uses the chosen index satisfies. LPs ask 'why this index?' — having 'benchmark + CAPM proxy' clearly stated in advance avoids the 'specified in advance' failure mode under GIPS.
